title: Five-class provenance of chatbot text in student writing and programming (FLoRA, RelianceScope): code, analysis log, statistics
description: Version 1.10.0. Code, a dated analysis log and statistics files for a study of verbatim uptake of chatbot text in students' graded project proposals (FLoRA Open Data IPS, 275 students). v1.1.0 added log entry R1: time-aware echo correction, third-source filter, clock check from chat-box keystrokes, validation against logged paste events, and extended analyses of grades and detection. v1.2.0 adds log entry R2: three open zero-shot AI-text detectors (log-likelihood, Fast-DetectGPT, Binoculars on Qwen2.5 models) evaluated against logged provenance at paragraph level, by first language, and sensitivity of the third-source threshold. All analyses are exploratory. No third-party data are redistributed. v1.3.0 adds log entry R3: attribution of each token of the submitted artefact to five provenance classes (chatbot-first, echo, shared source, typed, untraced insertion), applied to FLoRA and to the RelianceScope programming dataset with validation against human response-use codes and an unaided post-test; FLoRA detector reanalysis on typed vs untraced text (post hoc). Third-party data are not redistributed. v1.4.0 adds log entry R4: entry mode by edit size, validation of typed and untraced classes against logged pastes, chance baseline and conservative bounds for chatbot-first code, length-controlled validation against human codes, and a censored model of the post-test. v1.4.1 records the RelianceScope authors' permission to use the dataset with citation; no analyses changed. v1.5.0 adds log entry R5: within-document moves in the untraced class, token-level projection, clock distribution, segment-local entry rule, origin of echo text, timing baseline by class, code-aware tokenisation for the programming data, robustness of the grade model (multiple imputation, censoring, transformations, class shares) and of the post-test models (chance-corrected and reference-excluded uptake, task progress), detector thresholds, and a size-matched and semantic paraphrase check. v1.6.0 adds log entry R6, committed before its analyses ran, after earlier results were known: attribution with degraded logs (dialogue only, thinned editor snapshots), effect of every parameter choice on the main quantities, chance baseline by n-gram length, descriptive subdivision of the untraced class, origin of logged pastes, minimum detectable effects and simulated power of the outcome models, and a self-contained end-to-end demonstration on synthetic logs (demo/). No measure or class definition changed. v1.7.0 adds log entry R7, committed before its analyses ran, after earlier results were known: comparison of students with and without logged paste events, agreement of segment uptake with each human response-use code, a diagram of the routes by which text reaches the editor, and the class figure recomputed with the edit-size entry rule. No measure or class definition changed. v1.8.0 adds log entry R8, committed before its analyses ran, after earlier results were known: sensitivity of the grade analysis to misclassification of untraced text, equivalence tests, order of the echo and shared-source rules, agreement with retyped code, a label-noise ceiling for the human codes, a comparison with the LLM classifiers released with RelianceScope, post-test models with pre-activity covariates, numerical-Hessian standard errors for the censored models, and token-level five-class labels produced by the attribution of the 275 FLoRA proposals (CC BY 4.0). No measure or class definition changed. v1.9.0 renames the analysis files from PREREG_* to ANALYSIS_LOG_* (file names cited inside them updated, content otherwise unchanged; the entries record decisions made as the analysis proceeded and are not pre-registrations) and adds log entry R9: accuracy against simulated logs with known routes under clock offsets, snapshot thinning and paraphrase; an audit of sampled passages against keystrokes and chatbot-panel selections that the attribution does not use; echo split by entry mode and route; run time; thinning by class; entry threshold and paste window; a token-level entry variant added after the audit result for typed text; and a decomposition of the chance baseline for code. The primary measure is unchanged. v1.10.0 adds log entry R10, committed before its analyses ran: a benchmark with planted provenance fitted to the FLoRA logs, with per-class confusion, precision and recall and student-level error of U* under several snapshot resolutions; winnowing (MOSS-style) and greedy string tiling (JPlag-style) baselines on the benchmark and on both datasets; an online version of the attribution with agreement, latency per snapshot and memory; attribution of intermediate snapshots and a parameter table for RelianceScope; a label-noise ceiling over a range of error rates; and student-level intervals for the FLoRA paste checks. The primary measure is unchanged.
